kf: Drugs cause about 10–20% of acquired hyperpigmentation; colours and sites are clues.
**Minocycline**: blue-grey on scars, shins and sclera; **amiodarone**: slate-grey on sun-exposed face; **hydroxychloroquine**: grey-blue shins and palate.
Chemotherapy (bleomycin flagellate streaks, 5-FU), zidovudine (nails), clofazimine (red-brown), heavy metals (argyria).
Fixed drug eruption leaves round grey-brown patches at the same sites.
Stop or switch the drug with the prescriber; pigmentation fades slowly (months–years) or may be permanent; photoprotection.
myths: **"It'll go as soon as the drug stops"**: dermal pigment can persist for years.
patho_lead: Drugs pigment skin by **increasing melanin, depositing themselves, or forming drug–iron–melanin complexes**.

mech.t: Some drugs stimulate melanocytes (oral contraceptives in melasma, chemotherapy).
Drug or metabolites deposit in the dermis (amiodarone lipofuscin, gold, silver).
Drug, iron and melanin bind together in dermal macrophages (minocycline).
Inflammatory reactions leave melanin in the dermis (fixed drug eruption).

comp: Cosmetic distress; marker of cumulative dose (amiodarone).
